# 07 · The Land Rush (absorbs 16 · Expansionists)
Ground as the payoff: authority + border culture → more of everything. The Charter
posture's spine. Constraint: authority relief lives HERE, in Orders — trim it everywhere else.
Wins by: The Founder · The Twelve · The Most Cities.

**Tech:** Colonial Charters (Æra III) is the theme's one node — plain settler and founding bonuses; the overseas act arrives with The Astrolabe (see 13).

## Æra I
- Orders:
  - Boundary Stones — +30% border culture in every city.
  - Land Grants — Buying a hex costs 25% less · +40% border culture.
- Doctrines:
  - The Founders' Road — Your first 5 cities are founded with a free Monument, and new cities are joined to your nearest city by road.
  - Manifest of the Steppe — Settlers cost 40% less and never cost more than the first · every city demands +1 happiness.
- Deeds:
  - The Founder — Found eight cities of your own. Cities taken from others do not count.

## Æra II
- Orders:
  - Royal Surveyors — +50% border culture · buying a hex costs 25% less.
  - Provincial Governors — +3 authority capacity.
  - Vassalage — +2 authority capacity · a captured city costs one less authority.
  - The King's Table — +1 happiness for every 2 citizens in your capital.
  - Homestead Charters — Newly founded cities start with 2 more population.
  - Charter Towns — Newly founded cities are founded with a granary and a monument.
- Doctrines:
  - Hegemony — +1 authority capacity for each city you hold · a captured city costs one less authority.
- Religion: 
  - The Promised Land *(user's effect, named — pool TBD, likely follower)* — settlers trained in your cities carry an extra population, and the cities they found start with your religion.
- Great people: *(proposal)* The Founder's Legacy — while this legacy stands, cities you found start with +1 population.
- Deeds:
  - The Twelve — Hold twelve cities of six citizens or more.
  - The Surveyor — Buy twenty hexes of ground across the game.

## Æra III
- Tech:
  - the Stele of Laws re-homes to a new Æra III node — proposed name **The Charter Stones** (plain: unlocks the Stele and its authority) · *(needs your confirmation on which half renames — the node or the building)*
  - **connected cities gain +1 happiness** *(user)* — proposed home: The Imperial Post (the existing Æra III node, currently effectless after the Relay ruling — post roads making connected towns content is exactly its name).
- Orders: *(planned)* 
  - The King's Highway *(user)* — cities connected to the capital gain +1 happiness for every 3 cities you control.
  - The Colonial Office *(user — renamed: the TECH keeps 'Colonial Charters')* — settlers train 50% faster · cities founded more than 15 hexes from your capital cost 1 less authority.
  - The Prize Grounds *(user)* — cities settled on a luxury gain +2 happiness.
- Doctrines:
  - The Wandering Court *(moved from 08 by user ruling — a wide bonus)* — −15% to every yield in your capital · +3 food, production, science, culture and faith, and +3 happiness, in every city but your capital.
  - The Homestead Act *(proposal — wild)* — settlers no longer consume population · −1 happiness for every city you found thereafter. (Wide without gutting your towns; the bill arrives as contentment.)
  - The March Lords *(proposal)* — cities 12+ hexes from your capital gain +3 of every yield. (Distance becomes an asset — the anti-Hermit-Crown.)
  - The First Ring *(proposal)* — newly founded cities claim their entire first ring at founding. (Founding feels instantly real; borders stop crawling.)
  - The Twelve Banners *(proposal)* — +1 happiness in every city for each 3 cities you hold. (The wide happiness engine, stated plainly — the posture's relief budget under Entry LIV.)
  - The Founding Fever *(proposal — wild)* — a newly founded city's yields are doubled for its first 10 turns. (The rush made literal; snowball with a fuse.)
- Deeds:
  - The Most Cities — At the close of the age, the empire holding the most cities.
  - The Grand Satrapy — A race. Needs ten cities. The first empire to finish keeps a lasting step of contentment and of authority.

## Æra IV
- *(planned)* the overseas colony (with 11 and 13): settle the far landmass, an endeavour to plant a thriving colony
- Orders:
  - The Postal Union *(proposal, 🐫 crossover — shares The Yam's shape with 15)* — +1 science per pair of connected cities.
- Deeds:
  - The New World *(proposal, endeavour)* — a race: the first thriving overseas colony (a city of 8+ citizens on the far landmass).
  - The Broadest Realm *(proposal, reckoning)* — at the close of the age, the empire owning the most territory (hexes, not cities — the surveyor's crown).
